adversarial_review.findings:
## Verdict

The work is substantially sound. Every command in `plan/evidence/R1-19.json` reproduces exactly as claimed (test counts 9/5/6/4+1 ignored/4/2/3/3, plus 2 doc tests), both `compile_fail` doc tests fail for their *targeted* reason, and every whole-rule blinding I attempted was caught. I found no row marked `pass` that I can measure as failing, and no silencing. I did find **three surviving mutations** that show two rows are weaker than their evidence text asserts, and one class of coverage that is partial without being recorded as a gap.

All mutation work was done in a private copy at `/tmp/claude-1025/-home-infra-sj278-automonique/189dce1c-a957-463e-bb89-3fdb77b0d452/scratchpad/r119rev-3889236`. The repo is byte-identical to how I found it and still green (36 passed, 1 ignored). Note: the shared scratchpad `.../scratchpad/mut` is in active use by another agent — I moved off it.

## Per-row

| Row | Genuinely closed? |
|---|---|
| Surface coverage | **Partially.** Closed at class granularity (10/10, table matches evidence exactly: 5/4/44/0/4/23/0/0/1/0 = 81). Not closed at the granularity the contract asks for ("scanned-versus-total per surface class ... so partial coverage is visible instead of implied"). See D1, D2, D5. |
| Namespace enforcement | **Closed for 8 of 10 classes.** Vacuous for Module and Fixture (D1); misses the product's own unversioned protocol-name spelling (D2). Positive control on the real tree passes: appending `[features]\nlegacy-feature = []` to `crates/automonique-protocol/Cargo.toml` fails 3 tests. |
| Bidirectional inventory | **Closed.** One untested half (D4). |
| No escape hatch | **Closed to the contract's letter** ("proven by attempting each" — all three attempted, non-vacuously). The structural claim behind it is not enforced (D3). |
| Determinism | **Genuinely closed.** Strongest module: removing `distinct()`'s sort fails `the_scan_does_not_depend_on_the_order_the_tree_is_walked`, so the replacement for the useless earlier test is load-bearing, as the evidence claims. |
| Actionable output | **Genuinely closed.** |
| The gate can fail | **Genuinely closed.** |
| Authorized exceptions | **Genuinely closed.** `docs/product-plan/reference/migration-plan.md:90` really does name `legacyctl` as a forwarding entry point. |
| Quality | Honestly marked `fail`. `crates/automonique-lab/Cargo.toml` confirms no dependency on `automonique-protocol`, so the 2 failures cannot be this item's. |

## Defects, most severe first

**D1 — Module and Fixture enforcement is vacuous inside a namespaced crate.** `tests/namespace.rs:262-283` (`module_path`) and `:469-485` (fixture rule) record crate-qualified identifiers, and `src/namespace.rs:235-241` (`is_canonical`) then matches on the crate prefix. Every package in this workspace is `automonique-*`, so no module or fixture name can ever produce a finding.
Surviving mutation (repo copy, no source edits): create `crates/automonique-protocol/src/legacy_shim.rs`, `crates/automonique-protocol/src/legacy_area/mod.rs`, `crates/automonique-protocol/fixtures/legacy-corpus.json`. Three deliberately non-namespaced identifiers on two scanned surfaces; the scan counts them (module 44→46, fixture 1→2) and the suite stays green — **36 passed, 0 failed**. `surface_coverage::every_surface_rule_can_find_a_violation` (`:833`) conceals this because `seeded()` uses package `legacy-runner`, so its Module and Fixture "violations" (`legacy_runner::telemetry`, `legacy_runner::legacy-corpus`) fire off the *package* name, not the module/fixture stem. Partially disclosed: the evidence discloses the fixture case, not the module consequence.

**D2 — "schema and protocol names" is scanned for schemas only; protocol names are never scanned, and the gap is not recorded.** `tests/namespace.rs:290-317` (`schema_names`) requires a `/vN` suffix. This product's protocol names are dotted and *unversioned*: `crates/automonique-protocol/src/codec.rs:458-470` defines `ProtocolName` as "Dotted lowercase protocol name, such as `automonique.runner`" with a validator that rejects `/`, and `crates/automonique-protocol/src/tools.rs:47-53` declares five such identities in shipped source (`RESERVED_CAPABILITIES`) — none of which appear in the 23 scanned schemas.
Surviving mutation: add `crates/automonique-protocol/src/probe_names.rs` containing `pub const LEGACY_PROTOCOL: &str = "legacy.runner";` and `pub const LEGACY_CAPABILITY: &str = "legacy.workflow.execute";` — suite stays green, **36 passed**. The report says `schema: scanned, 23 found` with no denominator, so partial coverage inside a scanned class is exactly what the contract's "instead of implied" clause is aimed at.

**D3 — the structural "no escape hatch" test is defeated by a one-line rewrite.** `tests/namespace.rs:1368-1389` greps `src/namespace.rs` for seven literal spellings (`std::env`, `std::fs`, …).
Surviving mutation: change `src/namespace.rs:60-61` to `use std::{env, error::Error};` (contains none of the seven strings) and insert at the head of `NamespaceGate::run` (`src/namespace.rs:623`):
```rust
if env::var("NAMESPACE_GATE_BYPASS").is_ok() {
    return GateReport::default();
}
```
Result: **36 passed, 0 failed** with a working kill switch in the gate. With `NAMESPACE_GATE_BYPASS=1` set, **18 of 36 tests fail**, so the hatch is real. `an_environment_variable_cannot_disable_the_gate` (`:1302`) only probes 6 hard-coded names, so it does not close the hole either. The property holds in the code as shipped; the evidence's claim that it is proven structurally does not.

**D4 — the orphan direction's surface scoping is untested.** `src/namespace.rs:644-648` keys orphan detection on `(name, surface)`; replacing it with `!scanned.iter().any(|identifier| identifier.name == entry.name)` leaves the suite green (**36 passed**). Failure it would hide: inventory holds `(Binary, "legacyctl")`; the forwarding binary is deleted and a metric named `legacyctl` appears — the dead permission stops being reported, and only the metric finding shows. All three orphan tests (`:988`, `:1004`, `:1051`) use names absent from the whole scan, so none exercises the surface half.

**D5 — rule-internal blinding survives the lower-bound assertions.** `tests/namespace.rs:732-745` asserts counts as lower bounds with slack. ## Observations, not defects

- `is_canonical` gaining a third canonical spelling (`CANONICAL_DOT_PREFIX`, restricted to `SurfaceClass::Schema`) is a real behaviour change to a pre-existing method. It is disclosed in the evidence notes, tested against an expectation written out independently of `permits_dotted_namespace()` (`:929-930`), and is needed because the 23 dotted schema names predate this item and no migration contract authorizes renaming them. It nevertheless widens "in the namespace" by code change rather than by inventory entry, while the contract's Objective names only `automonique-*`/`automonique_*`. **This is a judgement call the owner should ratify, not something I can measure as false.**
- `.github/workflows/rust.yml` runs `cargo test --workspace --all-targets`, which excludes doc tests — so the two `compile_fail` proofs cited by "Actionable output" and "Authorized exceptions" never run in CI. Both properties are still enforced in CI by ordinary tests (`let [rename, inventory] = …` at `tests/namespace.rs:1182` and `:1207` is a compile-time arity check in a target CI does build).
- `SurfaceInventory`'s doc (`src/namespace.rs:376-377`) says an identifier filed under the wrong surface "is unrepresentable". True of `record`; not true of the crate, since `ScannedIdentifier::new` is public and the tests themselves file a metric at `rust/Cargo.toml`. Overstated, scoped enough to be defensible.

Both `compile_fail` doc tests fail for the property they target, not an artefact — flipping the fences to plain gives `error[E0061]: this function takes 3 arguments but 2 arguments were supplied` (line 20 block) and `error[E0527]: pattern requires 1 element but array has 2` (line 41 block), each with a paired passing example at lines 26 and 50. Neither owned file contains `#[allow]`, `todo!`, `unimplemented!`, `dbg!` or `unsafe`; `namespace::` is imported by no other crate, so the new private field on `GateReport` breaks no sibling.
